newsitem.title: CROATIA: Second earthquake hits Croatian coast.
newsitem.headline: Second earthquake hits Croatian coast.

text.p: An earthquake shook Croatia's Adriatic coast for the second time this month on Tuesday, triggering landslides and new damage to villages, officials said.

The Croatian Seismological Institute said the quake at 3.46 pm (1346 GMT) measured 5.5 on the Richter scale and struck the same Ston-Slano area near the historic city of Dubrovnik which suffered a 6.0 quake on September 5.
An official at the Dubrovnik alert centre reported minor landslides on the main coastal road and more damage to village houses.
So far it had no information if anyone had been injured in the quake, which was felt through much of Croatia and in the Bosnian capital of Sarajevo.

Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic asked the European Union (EU) last week for urgent help for the Ston area, saying the first quake had undone all work to repair severe damage suffered in the Croatian-Serb war of 1991.
One person was reported slightly injured in the first quake, which was followed by a series of aftershocks. Villagers were evacuated, although some pitched tents near their damaged homes.
